title: must / mustn't / have to / don't have to
grammarTitle: must / mustn't / have to / don't have to
grammarNote:
Четыре формы обязательности/необходимости:

① MUST — внутренняя обязанность (сам считаю нужным):
   "I must call my mother — she's worried." (сам решил)
   Используется для своих решений и строгих требований

② HAVE TO — внешняя обязанность (правила, законы):
   "I have to wear a uniform at work." (правило компании)
   "Students have to pass all exams." (требование вуза)

③ MUSTN'T — ЗАПРЕЩЕНО (нельзя делать):
   "You mustn't smoke here." (запрещено — это запрет!)
   ⚠️ Это НЕ то же самое что "don't have to"!

④ DON'T HAVE TO — НЕ ОБЯЗАН (нет необходимости, но можно):
   "You don't have to come if you're tired." (свободен выбирать)
   "I don't have to wear a tie." (необязательно)

💡 Главный контраст:
MUSTN'T = НЕЛЬЗЯ (запрещено)
DON'T HAVE TO = НЕ ОБЯЗАН (но можно если хочешь)

grammarExtra.title: must vs have to — source of obligation

rows.form: "must" — speaker's own authority / inner feeling
rows.example: I must study harder. (my own decision) / You must stop — it's dangerous.

rows.form: "have to" — external rule / someone else's authority
rows.example: I have to sign in at 11pm. (dormitory rule) / She has to wear a helmet. (law)

rows.form: In practice, both are often used interchangeably for rules
rows.example: You must attend. / You have to attend. (both acceptable for rules)

rows.form: "Must" is more formal / written; "have to" is more natural/spoken
rows.example: "You must bring ID." (official sign) vs "You have to bring ID." (someone telling you)

rows.form: "must" has no past form — use "had to" for the past
rows.example: She had to retake the exam. / We had to leave early. (NOT: she must study yesterday)

rows.form: In questions: "have to" is more common
rows.example: Do you have to sign in? (more natural) vs Must you sign in? (very formal)

grammarExtra.title: THE KEY CONTRAST: mustn't vs don't have to

rows.form: "mustn't" = FORBIDDEN — you are NOT allowed to do this
rows.example: You mustn't copy in exams. (it is against the rules — punishment)

rows.form: "don't have to" = NO OBLIGATION — it's your free choice
rows.example: You don't have to join a club. (it's optional — no pressure)

rows.form: These are OPPOSITES — do not confuse them!
rows.example: You mustn't drink alcohol. ✓ (it's forbidden) / You don't have to drink alcohol. ✓ (no one forces you)

rows.form: Common mistake: using "mustn't" when you mean "don't have to"
rows.example: You mustn't wear a uniform. ✗ (This means: it is FORBIDDEN to wear one!) / You don't have to wear one. ✓

rows.form: "needn't" = same as "don't have to" (British English, formal)
rows.example: You needn't attend the optional seminar. = You don't have to attend.

rows.form: Negative of "have to" = "don't/doesn't have to" (NOT "mustn't")
rows.example: She doesn't have to submit early. ✓ / She mustn't submit early. ✗ (wrong meaning: forbidden)

rows.form: Present: Do/Does + subject + have to + BASE?
rows.example: Do you have to sign in? / Does she have to attend every lecture?

rows.form: Past: Did + subject + have to + BASE?
rows.example: Did you have to retake the exam? / Did she have to submit early?

rows.form: Short answers
rows.example: Do you have to sign in? — Yes, I do. / No, I don't.

rows.form: "Must" questions (formal, rare)
rows.example: Must students attend all seminars? — Yes, they must.

rows.form: "Have to" vs "must" in questions: "have to" is more natural
rows.example: Do I have to bring a dictionary? (natural) vs Must I bring a dictionary? (very formal)

rows.form: Negative questions
rows.example: Don't you have to submit this today? / Doesn't she have to sign in?

grammarExtra.title: Modal verbs overview at A1.1 level

rows.form: can — ability or permission
rows.example: Can you help me? / Students can use the library.

rows.form: should — advice / recommendation
rows.example: You should study. / She should rest.

rows.form: must / have to — strong obligation
rows.example: You must attend. / She has to submit by Friday.

rows.form: mustn't — prohibition (forbidden)
rows.example: You mustn't cheat. / Students mustn't smoke inside.

rows.form: don't have to — no obligation (optional)
rows.example: You don't have to join a club. / He doesn't have to come.

rows.form: All modals + BASE form (no -s, no to, no -ing)
rows.example: She should go ✓ / She must go ✓ / She has to go ✓ (only "have to" has the form "has to" for he/she)

grammarTip:
Самая частая ошибка — путать mustn't и don't have to:

MUSTN'T = НЕЛЬЗЯ / ЗАПРЕЩЕНО:
"You mustn't park here." (штраф!)
"You mustn't copy homework." (нарушение правил)

DON'T HAVE TO = НЕ ОБЯЗАН / НЕОБЯЗАТЕЛЬНО:
"You don't have to park here." (можешь, но не обязан)
"You don't have to do extra homework." (по желанию)

💡 Тест: можно ли сделать без нарушения правил?
✅ Можно (просто не обязан) → don't have to
❌ Нельзя (нарушение) → mustn't

You ___ share your login details — it's a security rule.
Students ___ wear a uniform — there isn't one at WKU.

opts: You are not required to bring food.
You are not allowed to bring food.
You do not need to bring food.
exercises.correct: You are not allowed to bring food.

exercises.text: I ___ sign in at the dormitory after 11pm. It's a building rule.
exercises.hint: "Have to" = external obligation (a rule set by someone else, not your own choice).

exercises.text: She ___ submit the assignment by Friday. Her lecturer set the deadline.
exercises.hint: "Have to" 3rd person singular = "has to". External obligation set by the lecturer.

exercises.text: She ___ retake the exam last year because she failed.
exercises.hint: "must" has no past form. Use "had to" for past obligation.
"Have to" questions: Do/Does + subject + have to + BASE?

exercises.text: He ___ attend the optional session — it's his choice.
exercises.hint: "doesn't have to" = no obligation for he/she/it. Not "mustn't" (that would mean forbidden).

exercises.text: "You don't have to come to the party" means:
opts: You are forbidden from coming to the party.
You are not obliged to come — it is optional.
You cannot come to the party.
exercises.correct: You are not obliged to come — it is optional.
exercises.hint: "don't have to" = optional, no pressure. NOT a prohibition.

exercises.text: You ___ smoke inside the building — it's completely forbidden.
Which sentence uses "don't have to" correctly?
opts: You don't have to cheat — it's against the rules.
You don't have to attend the optional trip — but you're welcome to.
You don't have to graduate this year — or you'll be expelled.
You don't have to study — you must fail.
exercises.correct: You don't have to attend the optional trip — but you're welcome to.
exercises.hint: "don't have to" = optional, no pressure. Used for non-mandatory activities.

questions.text: Students ___ wear a uniform at WKU.
She ___ submit by Friday. It's her lecturer's rule.
questions.hint: "Has to" (3rd person external obligation): she + has to + BASE.

questions.text: "You mustn't attend" and "You don't have to attend" mean the same thing.
questions.hint: "mustn't attend" = forbidden. "don't have to attend" = optional. Completely different!

questions.text: She ___ retake the exam last year.
questions.hint: "must" has no past form → use "had to" for past obligation.
"Have to" question: Do + subject + have to + BASE?

questions.text: You ___ (not / share) your password with anyone.
questions.hint: "mustn't" = it is forbidden. mustn't + BASE form.

questions.text: "must" is used when the obligation comes from:
opts: The speaker's own authority or inner feeling
questions.correct: The speaker's own authority or inner feeling
questions.hint: "must" = the speaker feels it is necessary / their own strong sense of duty.

questions.text: He ___ wear a tie — it's optional at WKU.
questions.hint: "doesn't have to" = no obligation for he/she/it.

questions.text: "Have to" and "must" are identical in all situations.
questions.hint: "Must" = speaker's authority. "Have to" = external rule. Also, "must" has no past form, "had to" does.

questions.text: Students ___ join a club — but it is strongly recommended.
questions.hint: "don't have to" = optional (no one forces you).

questions.text: You ___ smoke inside — it's completely forbidden.

questions.hint: "must" + BASE form (no "to", no changes for 3rd person).
"needn't" = don't/doesn't have to = no obligation. British English equivalent.

questions.text: Spot the error: "You don't have to cheat — it's against the rules."
opts: "against the rules" should be "a good idea"
The sentence is fine as it is
questions.hint: "don't have to" means optional — but cheating is FORBIDDEN, so "mustn't" is correct.
